# Port Daddy LLM Full Context Index

## Product
Port Daddy is an always-on local daemon and control plane for coordinating multiple coding agents in the same repository.

Core capabilities:
- deterministic semantic identity -> port mapping
- session lifecycle with immutable notes
- distributed file claims and locks
- scoped pub/sub channels for inter-agent signaling
- salvage queue for crash recovery and work continuity
- harbor capability boundaries and DNS/tunnel primitives
- fleet orchestration for scheduled and trigger-based agent runs

## Docs Structure
- /docs                         : Documentation landing
- /docs/quickstart              : Install + first run
- /docs/guides/prompting-agents : Prompt engineering for coordinated fleets
- /docs/guides/templates        : Starter templates and command patterns
- /docs/guides/protocol         : Lifecycle/state/event model with diagrams
- /docs/features/*              : Concept pages
- /docs/cli/*                   : CLI reference
- /docs/sdk/*                   : TypeScript SDK reference
- /docs/mcp/*                   : MCP tool reference
- /docs/api                     : HTTP API reference

## Recommended grounding order for models
1) /docs
2) /docs/quickstart
3) /docs/guides/prompting-agents
4) /docs/guides/protocol
5) interface-specific reference pages (/docs/cli or /docs/sdk or /docs/mcp or /docs/api)

## Operational note
Use project-scoped identity and channel context when producing commands/examples for users.
